chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washsha' who said:

I asked Imam ar-Rida (peace be upon him): 'Does the earth remain without an Imam?' He said: 'No.' I said: 'We narrate traditions saying that it does not remain [without an Imam] except if Allah becomes angry with the people.' He said: 'It does not remain [without an Imam], otherwise it would sink.'

key_terms.إِمَام: Imam, the divinely appointed leader and proof of God on earth
key_terms.الْأَرْضُ: The earth/world, referring to the physical realm of existence
key_terms.لَسَاحَتْ: It would sink, a cosmological concept indicating the earth's instability without divine authority
key_terms.يَسْخَطَ اللَّهُ: Allah becomes angry, referring to divine displeasure or wrath

ai.seo_question: Why does the earth not remain without an Imam according to Imam ar-Rida?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Nu'mani's *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam ar-Rida (AS) affirms the perpetual necessity of the Imam (Hujjah) for the world's stability, countering reports that link the absence of an Imam solely to divine wrath. He clarifies that the earth would literally 'sink' or collapse without an Imam, establishing the Imam as a cosmic pillar (*Hujjah*) essential for the existence of the world, not merely a judge for its inhabitants. This underscores the Shia doctrine of *Imamat* as a fundamental ontological requirement for creation's continuity.
